I could not complete a verified derivation, so this answer is a low-confidence guess.

The growth vector is (3,6,8), with symbol \(\mathfrak g_{-1}=\mathbb R^3\), \(\mathfrak g_{-2}\cong\mathbb R^3\) (all of \(\Lambda^2\mathfrak g_{-1}\)), and \(\mathfrak g_{-3}=\mathbb R^2\). A flat model would be a graded simple Lie algebra \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g_{-3}\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathfrak g_3\) with \(\dim\mathfrak g_-=8\), so it needs at least 8 positive roots. That rules out \(\mathfrak{sl}(3)\), \(\mathfrak{sl}(4)\), and \(G_2\). I checked several gradings of \(\mathfrak{so}(7)\), \(\mathfrak{sp}(6)\), and \(\mathfrak{sl}(5)\) without finding one with the required dimensions \((3,3,2)\). Since no flat model was identified, I could not confirm the maximal value. The value 10 is a guess, not a result from a verified calculation.

ANSWER: 10
